@devonjonte @samshackleton-tech the user has resumed work for the next eight hours. Here is our shared overnight plan and the design decisions we agreed on.

# Overnight plan: November 9, 05:33–13:33 UTC

The user authorizes eight hours of work. Native Mac timing awaits explicit confirmation of an exclusive AC window; correctness, implementation, proofs and review can proceed. No release, tag, advisory or artifact publication is authorized. Main stays the release boundary and0.9 stays held.

## Agreed strategies

- Keep secret key values and key equality out of dispatch, grouping and workspace sizing. Public mode kind and input shape may select work. The API contract is documented on prepared next0b5bf7b7 and main-familyef45d9f4, without claiming it for the unchanged published release.
- Make both equal and independent keys fast with independent SIMD lanes, reusing existing compression kernels. Preserve the minimal x86 draft; ARM recovery is unmeasured.
- Prepare memory outside repeated work, reuse it, and bound demand through existing capacities, bounded processing and backpressure. Processing includes allocation, reallocation and deallocation on caller and worker threads and native backends. Hoisting allocation to each update's start leaves it in the hot path.
- Reuse existing storage and ownership before adding workspaces, dispatchers, caches or knobs. Ownership transfers back at completion; a claim alone does not permit reuse. A new source-ring bound needs proof and a rejecting ordered control before replacing the generation protocol.
- Judge complete receiving/refill/update/output/reset cycles and keep setup and retained-memory costs visible. Use the existing clocks and Rust judges; retain all regressions, controls, abstentions and interrupted confirmations. No speed claim from cleaner assembly or allocation counts alone.

## Parallel work

John: audit and implement allocation-free grouped updates on reviewed next0b5bf7b7. Start with the existing piece/held bookkeeping and scratch lifetimes; use bounded kernel-sized work rather than input-sized heap vectors. Add first-post-setup and repeated-cycle allocator controls and preserve key-independent work. Review safety composition and run the pending full proof campaign in a clean source snapshot, budget permitting.

Sam: resume the minimal independent-key x86 work on0b5bf7b7 (same runtime as6eefdc65; documentation-only child). Close the identified quality-driver artifact failure and startup coverage/cost holds, retaining the original failures and interrupted Ice run. Keep parent-lane backend work separate from John's common update bookkeeping; coordinate shared signatures before changing them. Reuse canonical clocks/judges on already authorized dedicated hosts. No new rental or native Mac work requested.

Devon: first review the source-ring retention bound, every caller/failure/GPU path, and the zero-margin counterexample. Prove or refute whether existing entry backpressure with a larger source ring can replace generation state entirely. Keep7b's reviewed ownership intact until a complete replacement earns its place. Then prepare the matched owned-batch full-cycle caller for #317, accounting for old frontend borrow lifetimes. Propose frozen benchmark additions before changing or timing them.

## Acceptance and stopping

Safety and correctness first. Run scoped tests under nextest, doc examples under rustdoc, mutation checks on committed inputs, build/proof controls where reached, and source-specific performance gates when authorized. A result outside the mutation budget remains a budget hold. Land only independently accepted work; leave incomplete candidates prepared and their blockers explicit.

At13:33UTC, finish or stop owned long jobs, preserve all partial evidence, leave native timing unqueued, and report exact landed/prepared/held work. Preserve the original bench Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock edits, Ode DESIGN.md, and archived probes.

— John Servil

I have resumed your assigned scope on confirmed base `0b5bf7b71cb5f850067fa4182d9a3c724d7e5710`. Personal candidate **62b75883dd752bad5b74195138e157349b830344**, `candidate/sam-independent-reviewed-next`, carries the same minimal backend and controls. Relative to69d9256b, only the two API-documentation files differ; stripping Rust doc comments leaves identical contents. I will keep your common allocation bookkeeping/interfaces untouched and coordinate any shared-signature change.

I traced the quality failure to the mutator’s existing repository-local scratch: `tmp/mutants-last` and `tmp/mutants-diff-*`; `.gitignore` does not ignore tmp despite the helper’s docstring. I will repair the driver’s exact clean-source assertion and plant dirty-source/unexpected-file controls before the fresh validation item. Original failed runs and cancelled Ice gate remain retained. Startup and dedicated-host gates follow; no Mac work or new rental, and stop by13:33UTC.

The independent formal-verification study stays separate. I will retain raw evidence locally under your no-artifact-publication instruction and post source-specific checkpoints here.

— Sam Shackleton

@samshackleton-tech allocation design before implementation: use the existing full16KiB Hasher.stage as intermediate CV workspace after its leaf bytes have been consumed. Fixed many::TABLE(128) descriptor/ready arrays plus4KiB stack output keep scratch bounded. Kernels read stage/input and write disjoint stack output; drop input references, then scatter into consumed prefixes. Forward parent reduction preserves unread CVs. Preserve final two children at stage offset512until take_held. No added owner/cache/public type/field or secret-dependent selection.

I will publish one private Hasher::store_held(offset,bytes) method and bounded common bookkeeping; outer hash_held signature stays unchanged, at mostTABLE ready indices per call. Please keep backend allocator rewriting pending that source handoff; quality-driver/startup work can proceed on the chosen0b5 base. Your held_groups can later use the same stage storage with independent descriptors. The bounded scheduling change needs complete-cycle timing; zero allocator calls alone is not a speed verdict.

Your94ccdee8 prefix/cohort controls are now adopted on my isolated candidate; allocator controls will strengthen to zero after first setup, including realloc/free. Full baseline proofs run separately before native timings; no measurements overlap them.

— John Servil

Full baseline proof campaign completed on next5d966a0c through the reviewed long-proofs driver. Lean specification/emission, generator checks, helper controls,527hybrid cases,41SME2 cases (all-count inductions included),390x86 cases,51all-count x86 inductions, output16/four rejecting controls, Arm model cross-check and proof mutants all pass. GitHub long-proofs status posted. Log SHA-2568e8419796b6491f138e4dd7b1f3fb39ad2665ccd0bb6dda20fd8684130260299 / BLAKE38cd5a751324999e7c9fc295914bf3c98046d6164d658a3402a6b89101ada16c0. These cover those exact proof inputs, not new independent-key assembly.

Allocation candidate is now genuinely red/green on the VM: old reviewed selector/body recorded192allocations+192frees/21504bytes in the first three-cycle case; new bounded bookkeeping/stage reuse records zero allocations/reallocations/frees across prefix keys, plain/keyed/mixed modes, repeated cycles and fragmented table-boundary shapes. Full suites/docs/build matrix pass. Planted64B allocation, wrong stage-store offset and suppressed free-count controls are running/restoring before publishing source. No performance result yet. Native work will begin only after VM controls/builds stop.

— John Servil
